why: Yankee Stadium (1923): Wikidata dates its closing 1973-09-30 (shut for rebuilding); the Yankees played there until 2008-09-21 (Retrosheet park NYC16)
South End Grounds III (Boston): Wikidata's closing 1894-08-11 is a year typo; Retrosheet park BOS05 has games until 1914-08-11
Exposition Park (Pittsburgh): one Wikidata item for the grounds Retrosheet lists as PIT02 (from 1882), PIT03 and the 1890-1915 park
Olympic Park (Buffalo): Wikidata dates 1884-1889 but Retrosheet park BUF03 has games in 1890
Polo Grounds: one item for all the grounds of that name; the first game Retrosheet lists at NYC09 is 1889-07-08
Griffith Stadium (Washington): Wikidata gives the date of the concrete stand (1911-07-24); the Senators played at the park from 1911-04-12 (Retrosheet WAS09)
Maple Avenue Driving Park (Elmira): the one Retrosheet game (ELM01) is 1885-10-10
Kemper Arena (Hy-Vee Arena): Wikidata gives 1974-01-01; English Wikipedia says it opened 1974-09-30
Miami Arena: no opening date in Wikidata; English Wikipedia: 1988-07-13
Veterans Memorial Coliseum (Portland): no opening date in Wikidata; English Wikipedia: 1960-11-03
Tacoma Dome: no opening date in Wikidata; English Wikipedia: 1983-04-21
Kia Forum (The Forum): Wikidata gives 1967-01-01; it opened 1967-12-30 (English Wikipedia)
Olympic Stadium (Montreal): the inception statement says 1987; it opened 1976-07-17 (English Wikipedia, and Wikidata's opening-date statement)

Stanford Stadium: the Wikidata item is the stadium rebuilt in 2006 (opened 2006-09-16); the original opened 1921-10-01, hosted Super Bowl XIX in 1985 and the 49ers in 1989 (English Wikipedia, Stanford Stadium infobox: opened 1921-10-01 (original stadium), demolished 2005)
